principles: Fail closed unless a git-backed signed workspace is explicit and verifiable.
Keep metadata persistence and material signing roots distinct but mechanically bound.
Prefer a narrow explicit gitRoot binding path over arbitrary nested repository discovery.
Do not convert local reviewer evidence into Authority Server proof.
drivers: ClawCreek needs an operator repair path beyond clearer not_git_repo diagnostics.
review_run_start and later REVIEW evidence consumers must agree on the signed material root.
Existing direct REVIEW behavior in ordinary git-backed repos must continue to work.
High-risk lifecycle evidence changes require regression tests for negative controls.

options.name: A: Shared resolver plus explicit gitRoot binding
pros: Solves wrapper-root projects without guessing nested repos.
Keeps implementation scope smaller than a new attachment command.
Can feed story_resolve and review_run_start from one contract.
cons: Does not provide a full story_attach_worktree command yet.
Requires careful tests for metadataRoot and signedWorkspaceRoot separation.

options.name: B: Add story_attach_worktree first
pros: Provides a direct per-story repair path.
Can express arbitrary existing linked worktrees.
cons: Requires branch/worktree ownership policy decisions not needed for the minimal ClawCreek fix.

options.name: C: Only improve diagnostics further
cons: Leaves wrapper-root users unable to start reviewer runs.
Does not satisfy the INIT reviewer blocker requiring an explicit binding path.

chosen: A: Shared resolver plus explicit gitRoot binding
rationale: Choose A because it fixes the observed correctness issue with the narrowest explicit binding path: metadataRoot remains the story store, gitRoot provides signedWorkspaceRoot, and unresolved wrapper roots still fail closed. story_attach_worktree can be a later enhancement after branch/path policy is designed.

preMortem.scenario: Implementation silently signs a nested repo just because cwd is inside it.
preMortem.trigger: A developer tests only a single nested repo wrapper project.
preMortem.consequence: A multi-repo wrapper can sign the wrong material root.
preMortem.mitigation: Resolver requires metadataRoot git root, story worktree, or explicit gitRoot; tests cover wrapper root plus nested repo without gitRoot as fail-closed.

preMortem.scenario: review_run_start succeeds but pass/finding freshness checks use a different root.
preMortem.trigger: Only the start command is updated while consumers still recompute from ctx.root.
preMortem.consequence: REVIEW gate can accept or reject evidence inconsistently.
preMortem.mitigation: Persist workspaceBinding and include consumer/tamper tests for review_pass_set/finding_add freshness behavior.

preMortem.scenario: Local host review is overstated as Authority completion.
preMortem.trigger: Documentation or status output reuses Authority terms for local review-run evidence.
preMortem.consequence: Users may believe production completion is receipt-backed when it is only local CLI evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Tests and wording keep receiptVerified, productionDone, authorityDone, and fullAuthorityDone false without verified gate_decision receipts.
